transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this... I just, well, I came in because I've been having a little trouble with, um, worrying, I guess? I mean, I know everyone worries, and I don't want to sound like I'm overreacting, but it just feels like once a thought starts, I can't seem to... shelve it in my mind. 

Like, if I start thinking about my mother getting up in the middle of the night, or a grant report I'm working on at the library, or even just whether I missed some small detail at work... the thought just kind of stays there. I try to be organized, you know? I make lists and try really hard to redirect myself, but it just doesn't seem to work like it should. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

Can you tell me if you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that bother you a lot — like thoughts that are intrusive, maybe even disturbing, and that you try to get rid of or suppress?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, the thoughts I get stuck on aren't really... disturbing, or bad. I would hate for you to think I'm having strange or inappropriate thoughts, or anything like that! 

It's really just the mundane things, like I mentioned—the library budget, or making sure the special collections are locked properly, or my mom's health. They bother me mostly just because my brain won't turn them off, but they aren't... scary or weird. I just worry a lot about doing a good job and making sure everything is taken care of. 

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most days, even when there isn't a specific reason or trigger for it?

Um, well... I suppose I do, yes. I really try to keep a positive attitude, and I don't want you to think I'm just falling apart or anything, because I do keep up with my responsibilities! But... over this past year, it feels like the worrying has sort of... spread? 

It used to just be about my mother’s safety, which makes sense, right? But now it's... well, it's finances, and staff decisions at the library, and deadlines, and keeping up with the house. I even worry constantly about whether I’m being a good daughter to her. It just feels like even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel, even if there isn't a big, obvious reason for it. 

I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed any physical signs or symptoms when you're feeling this way, like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, irritability, or trouble concentrating?

Um... well, I suppose sleep has been a little bit of a challenge lately. I mean, I don't want to complain, because I know everyone gets tired, and I really do try to push through it at work! But... when I go to bed, I tend to just lie there, sort of... replaying everything that happened during the day, and then trying to plan for any possible problem that might come up tomorrow. 

And then, if I happen to wake up and hear my mother moving around in the night—which is completely normal, of course—I just... I get so wide awake. I'll be up for an hour or two just thinking, and by the time I get to the library in the morning, I feel like I haven't really rested at all. 

I'm still getting my work done, though! I promise I'm not letting it affect my job performance. But... yes, I guess the sleep thing is a bit of an issue. Is it normal to feel that way when you have a lot on your plate?
How long have you been feeling this way with the constant worrying and trouble sleeping?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little over a year now. Maybe about a year and two months? 

I really don't want it to sound like I'm complaining about her, because I love having her with me, and it's absolutely my duty to care for her! But... it started right around the time my mother moved into my home. She had a fall, you see, and it just made sense for her to come live with me so I could keep an eye on things. 

I really thought I'd have adjusted to the new routine by now, and I feel a little silly that I'm still struggling with it. I mean, it's been over a year, I should have a handle on it, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can for her without falling behind at work. 

Is it... is it okay that it's taking me this long to get used to it? I hope you don't think I'm just being overly sensitive about the whole situation.
Have you been feeling more tired or low on energy lately, even after a night of not sleeping well?

Um, actually... no, I don't think I've really noticed feeling low on energy. I mean, I know I just said I haven't been sleeping perfectly, but during the day I really make a point to just keep going! 

I don't want to be the sort of person who drags their feet at work or at home, so I just... push through. If anything, I almost feel a bit keyed up most of the time, like I always need to be doing something or checking on something. So I wouldn't say I feel sluggish at all. 

I hope that makes sense? I just really try my best to stay productive and not let anyone down, so I don't really give myself the time to feel tired. Is it normal to feel sort of wired like that instead of exhausted?
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly and reaches a peak within minutes, like a panic attack?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I've ever had anything quite like that. I mean, I certainly get nervous, and sometimes my heart might flutter a little if I think I've forgotten something important for my mother or at the library. But... an intense fear like a panic attack? No, I don't think so. 

I'm usually pretty good at keeping my composure. I really try not to let things escalate to that point, because I know people are relying on me to be steady. I wouldn't want to cause a scene or worry anyone, you know? 

So, no sudden peaks of fear or anything. Just the constant sort of... buzzing worry in the background. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I'm glad I haven't had one, but I want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Has this constant worrying started to interfere with your daily life, like making it harder to enjoy things, focus on tasks, or spend time with others?

Well, um... I really try my absolute hardest not to let it affect anyone else. I want to be completely present for my mother and my friends, of course. But... at work... 

I really hate to even admit this, because I take so much pride in my job at the library, but I guess it has been making it a bit harder to focus lately. I've started missing these small, but, well, kind of important details. And... oh, this is so embarrassing, I almost didn't want to mention it... but we had a grant presentation recently, and I just... I sort of froze up. I actually had to hand off parts of it to a colleague right in the middle of it. 

That is just so incredibly unlike me. I always want to be a strong, reliable role model for my staff, and lately I've just been worrying if... if I can even keep leading my team well when my mind is so scattered. 

I hope you don't think I'm doing a terrible job or that I'm incompetent. I really am trying my best to keep everything running smoothly and not let anyone down. Is... is it normal to have a slip-up like that when you just have a lot on your plate? I hope I'm answering your question properly.
Do you often feel restless or like you're constantly on edge, as if you can't fully relax or settle down?

Um, restless... well, I wouldn't say I'm restless, exactly. I mean, I do like to stay busy! There's always so much to do at the library, and then checking in on my mother, so it's actually quite helpful that I don't just sit around. 

I guess... maybe sometimes I feel a tiny bit on edge, like I mentioned before, just wanting to make sure I haven't forgotten anything important. But I wouldn't want you to think I'm pacing the halls or unable to sit still or anything like that. I can definitely sit and read a book or watch a show if I really try to. It's just that my mind might still be running through my to-do list while I'm doing it. 

I really try to be productive with that energy, though. I don't want to seem like I'm just frantic for no reason. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I feel. It's perfectly fine to just be a very driven person, right?
Would you say that your worrying about things like work, family, or health happens on most days, and has been going on that way for at least six months or more?

Well, um... yes, I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it is most days. But I really wouldn't want you to think I've always been this... scattered. I actually used to be very good at leaving my work at work and just relaxing at home. 

It really only started getting to this constant level about... oh, I'd say a year and two months ago. My mother had a bit of a fall, and, well, I had her move into my home right after that so I could keep a proper eye on her and take care of things. I just want to be a good daughter and make sure she's safe, you know? So naturally, since she moved in, there's just been a lot more to juggle every single day. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound completely incapable that it's been going on for over a year now. It's just... it's a very big adjustment, taking on a caregiving role on top of managing the library. It's perfectly normal to have an extended period of worrying when you have a major life change like that, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the correct timeline and answering your question properly.
